title: Content-addressable quant artifact chain-of-custody and deterministic rehydration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Calibration runs for FP8/INT8 produce artifacts (scale tables, per-channel stats, quant profiles, calibration seeds and datasets) that are hard to trace, validate, and revert. Non-deterministic calibration or missing provenance causes production regression after model rollouts. Goal: Build a content-addressable artifact scheme plus a chain-of-custody envelope so any quant artifact can be deterministically rehydrated, validated against golden evals, and safely rolled back if needed.

Scope: Implement hashing and canonical serialization for all calibration artifacts; sign envelopes with service keys; store artifacts in the CAS (content-addressable store) with immutable tags; add rehydrate tool that reproduces an artifact deterministically given the envelope; integrate a lightweight validation pipeline that runs a subset of golden prompts and per-layer differential checks before traffic cutover.

Design details:
- Canonical serialization: stable JSON with sorted keys + binary blobs (scale tables) base64-encoded. Define canonical layout for: quant_profile.json, calibration_metadata.json, dataset_manifest.json, seed_state.bin.
- Hashing: use BLAKE3-256 over canonical bytes. Hash components individually (profile blob, dataset snapshot id, tool version) and compute an aggregate manifest hash. Store component hashes in the manifest.
- Envelopes: create a signed envelope (service signing key via KMS) that contains: manifest hash, component hashes, calibration tool git commit, runtime build_id, deterministic seed, environment fingerprint (driver versions, CUDA, OS, cpu micro arch), dataset snapshot reference, and human-readable changelog. Envelopes are append-only and immutable.
- CAS and tags: write artifacts into the CAS at /cas/<hash>. Support lightweight tags that map to a manifest hash but are immutable once published (tag creation requires a signed tag message). For rollbacks, create a new tag that points to an earlier manifest and publish via the control plane.
- Deterministic rehydration: rehydrate tool fetches all components from CAS and validates component hashes; sets environment variables and RNG seeds; runs a deterministic calibration replay mode that avoids non-deterministic accelerated kernels (fall back to deterministic kernel paths if needed) and produces an identical profile hash.
- Validation harness: run a staged validation pipeline: (1) smoke test: binary compatibility check and manifest signature verification; (2) golden eval: run 200 representative prompts through the quantized model and compute token-level and semantic metrics; (3) per-layer diff: compute L2/amax differences for activation ranges compared to baseline; (4) performance check: latency and memory SLOs under a synthetic load.
- Rollback strategy: canary rollout to 1% traffic for 1 hour with continuous golden evals; if regression detected, automated rollback tag mapping switches to prior manifest and a rollback incident is opened with audit trail. Manual rollback requires Product or SRE approval.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canonical serializer and BLAKE3 hashing library implemented with tests proving byte-identical outputs across runs and machines.
- Envelopes signed by KMS with visible verification in console.
- Rehydrate tool reproduces a known reference artifact (round-trip test) and returns the same aggregate manifest hash.
- Validation harness runs automatically in CI and on release pipelines; thresholded alarms for regressions.
- Console shows artifact lineage and provides a one-click rollback that creates a signed rollback tag and records the incident.

Non-goals: full CA/PKI rotation work (we only use KMS signing initially), long-term archival policies (handled by storage team), and full reproducibility across heterogeneous GPUs with different micro-architectures (we document limitations and require hardware tags in the envelope).
